title: Extension of a mathematical analogy between vortical flows without surface tension and irrotational capillary flows
summary: In a recent paper, a mathematical analogy was found between two physically distinct classes of two-dimensional free boundary problems in inviscid fluid mechanics. One class involves free surface flows with constant vorticity in the bulk but without boundary surface tension, the other comprises free surface flows without vorticity in the bulk but with non-zero boundary surface tension (capillarity). Several examples were given of pairs of physically-distinct free boundary problems that amount to solving the same mathematical problem, albeit with the possibility of a single constraint arising…
